target: P(season total ends strictly below 1363.0 mm | rainfall through week w)
small_sample_note: Only 3 of 26 seasons ended below the 1,363.0 mm payment line. Averages, bootstrap intervals, and the calibration table describe this sample. They are not a test of statistical significance.
selection_rule: Lowest mean Brier score across weeks 4, 8, 12, 16 and 21. A gap of 0.005 or less is a tie, broken by simplicity: rule, logistic, analog_raw, analog_scaled, lognormal, gamma, v1_no_temp, v1. Per-year plots were not used. Climatology is not a candidate.
selection_bias: The winner was chosen from 8 candidates on the same 26 seasons, 3 of them positive. That score is optimistically biased.

chosen.note: Bootstrap over seasons of the already computed leave-one-out Brier scores. Not a refit, and not a significance test. Only 3 seasons are positive.

rule.note: Bootstrap over seasons of the already computed leave-one-out Brier scores. Not a refit, and not a significance test. Only 3 seasons are positive.

lead_time.note: Earliest week is any week 1-21, not only the five checkpoints. A false alarm is a season that finished on or above the line and still reached p_relief >= 0.5.

calibration.note: Empty or very small bin. 26 seasons, 3 of them below the line.

trend.trend_note: Ordinary least squares on 26 season totals. The p-value is reported and is not a claim that the trend is real. One or two seasons move the slope.

below_the_line_by_window.note: 10 seasons. Too few to call a change in drought frequency.

dry_spells.definition: A dry day is strictly below 1 mm. A long spell is at least as long as the median longest spell of the seasons that finished below the payment line. This does not change the trigger. A season-total trigger can miss a damaging dry spell.
